whatItIs.text: Sodium chloride — the only rock humans eat, the source of one of the basic tastes, and the original food preservative.

historyNote.text: The earliest evidence of salt processing is around 6000 BC, when people in present-day Romania boiled spring water for salt and a Chinese salt works began at about the same time; what may be Europe's first city, Solnitsata in Bulgaria, was a salt mine supplying the Balkans from 5400 BC.

howToChoose.text: Table salt (with anti-caking) for baking, flaky or kosher salt for seasoning by hand — the crystal size changes how salty a pinch tastes; iodised salt matters where iodine deficiency is a risk.

storage.text: Keep dry and sealed — salt keeps indefinitely. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Salt never spoils: season pasta water, crust roasts, and finish dishes with it; clumped salt loosens with a toast-oven dry-out.

substitutions.note: a tablespoon of flakes weighs far less than a tablespoon of fine salt
